domain: Criminal Justice / Political Philosophy / Constitutional Law
topic_summary: Analysis of capital punishment as a contested kernel where the state's authority to execute is read through three incompatible interpretive frameworks: retributive justice (execution as moral restoration), deterrence (execution as crime prevention instrument), and abolition (execution as impermissible state violence). Each reading instantiates a structurally different constraint with distinct beneficiary/victim sets and extractiveness profiles.

key_entities: State execution authority (monopoly on legitimate lethal force)
Victims' families (claimed beneficiaries under retribution reading)
Future potential victims (claimed beneficiaries under deterrence reading)
Wrongfully convicted (victims under all readings, magnitude varies)
key_tensions: Retributive closure vs utilitarian prevention (incompatible justificatory grounds)
State sovereignty vs individual inviolability (authority to kill vs right not to be killed)
Procedural legitimacy vs substantive prohibition (can-we-do-it-fairly vs should-we-do-it-at-all)
key_absences: International law constraints (most peer nations abolished; U.S. exceptionalism unexamined)
Execution method evolution (lethal injection drug shortages forcing return to older methods; reveals scaffold instability)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The state's claimed authority to execute convicted offenders as legitimate exercise of sovereign power
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Legislative enactment plus judicial review; legitimacy grounded in constitutional text (Eighth Amendment 'cruel and unusual' standard) and democratic mandate

readings.commitment: Execution restores moral balance by imposing proportionate punishment for heinous crimes
readings.authority_grounding: Retributive justice theory; lex talionis tradition; victim-centered moral restoration
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victims' families enter beneficiary set; executed offender is legitimate cost; high ε from moral-restoration requirement (cannot substitute imprisonment); wrongful execution is tragic error but does not invalidate framework

readings.commitment: Execution prevents future murders by raising the cost of capital crimes
readings.authority_grounding: Utilitarian calculus; Beccaria deterrence theory; public safety mandate
readings.expected_structural_delta: Future potential victims enter beneficiary set; executed offender is instrumental cost; moderate ε from deterrence-efficacy requirement (can substitute if life-without-parole deters equally); wrongful execution is utilitarian loss requiring error-rate minimization

readings.commitment: State execution is categorically impermissible regardless of crime severity or procedural safeguards
readings.authority_grounding: Human dignity inviolability; international human rights law; Eighth Amendment evolving standards
readings.expected_structural_delta: All executed persons enter victim set (including guilty); no legitimate beneficiaries (retribution/deterrence rejected as justifications); very high ε from categorical prohibition (no substitution possible; life imprisonment is qualitatively different); wrongful execution is proof of systemic illegitimacy

axes.human_readable: Retributive Justice Reading (Execution as Moral Restoration)
axes.structural_delta: Execution restores moral balance through proportionate punishment; victims' families are primary beneficiaries
axes.primary_observable: Victim impact statement prevalence in capital sentencing; public support for execution-as-closure
axes.selection_reason: Distinct beneficiary structure (victims' families); high ε from non-substitutability of moral restoration claim

axes.human_readable: Deterrence Instrument Reading (Execution as Crime Prevention)
axes.structural_delta: Execution prevents future murders by raising cost of capital crimes; future potential victims are beneficiaries
axes.primary_observable: Deterrence study methodologies; murder rate differentials between death penalty and abolitionist jurisdictions
axes.selection_reason: Different beneficiary set and ε profile from retributive reading; utilitarian vs deontological grounding

axes.human_readable: Categorical Prohibition Reading (Execution as Impermissible State Violence)
axes.structural_delta: State execution is categorically impermissible; all executed persons are victims regardless of guilt
axes.primary_observable: International abolitionist treaty ratifications; Eighth Amendment evolving standards doctrine
axes.selection_reason: Highest ε; inverts victim set (includes guilty); categorical prohibition vs conditional justification

axes.human_readable: Wrongful Execution Risk (Irreversible Error in Fallible System)
axes.structural_delta: Execution forecloses error correction; wrongful execution rate is non-zero and unknowable
axes.primary_observable: DNA exoneration rates; post-execution evidence discoveries; appellate reversal rates
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: affects all three readings but does not constitute independent reading of kernel; captured as omega_error_rate_unknowability

axes.human_readable: Racial Disparity as Extraction (Disproportionate Black/Latino Death Sentences)
axes.structural_delta: Death penalty application exhibits racial disparities in charging, sentencing, and victim-race effects
axes.primary_observable: Death row demographics vs general population; victim-race sentencing differentials
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: high ε but operates as implementation-layer snare rather than kernel reading; captured in omega_disparity_as_implementation_vs_essence

axes.human_readable: Execution Method Scaffold (Lethal Injection Drug Shortage Instability)
axes.structural_delta: Preferred execution method depends on pharmaceutical supply chains; shortages force reversion to older methods
axes.primary_observable: State execution protocol changes; drug manufacturer boycotts; botched execution rates
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: scaffold instability reveals legitimacy fragility but does not constitute kernel reading

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Affects all readings but does not constitute independent kernel reading; error rate is input to each reading's constraint calculus rather than separate interpretive commitment
Implementation-layer extraction rather than kernel-level reading; operates within retributive/deterrence frameworks rather than offering third interpretive ground

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Lethal injection drug shortage forcing protocol changes
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Reveals legitimacy fragility but does not constitute kernel reading; method instability is symptom of deeper contested authority

omegas.description: Wrongful execution rate is structurally unknowable (cannot exhume and retry). Each reading handles this differently: retributive treats as tragic but non-invalidating error; deterrence requires error-rate minimization in utilitarian calculus; abolition treats any error as proof of categorical impermissibility. The unknowability itself may be a fourth reading (epistemic-humility prohibition).
omegas.source: Deferred axis wrongful_execution_risk + Dark Matter Probe 2

omegas.description: Is racial disparity an implementation flaw (fixable through better procedures) or essence of the practice (unfixable because discretion is load-bearing)? If essence, it collapses deterrence reading (cannot deter if application is arbitrary) and retributive reading (cannot restore balance if racially selective). Abolition reading absorbs this as additional proof.
omegas.source: Deferred axis racial_disparity_extraction + Dark Matter Probe 3

omegas.description: U.S. is only Western democracy retaining death penalty. Is this exceptionalism (legitimate sovereignty) or isolation (drift from evolving human rights norms)? Abolition reading treats international consensus as evidence of evolving standards; retributive/deterrence readings treat as irrelevant to domestic constitutional authority. Unexamined in extraction.

Retributive reading assumes victims' families benefit from execution-as-closure. Empirical evidence shows heterogeneity: some families oppose execution, some report closure from execution, some report no closure. If beneficiary set is empty or contested, retributive reading loses its justificatory ground. Requires empirical decomposition.

If life-without-parole deters equally to execution (contested empirical claim), deterrence reading collapses to retributive reading or abolition reading depending on whether non-deterrence justification is accepted. Deterrence reading's moderate ε depends on this substitutability claim holding false.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: abolition_reading classified as mountain (categorical prohibition grounded in human dignity inviolability) but this may be piton of evolving moral consensus rather than physical/logical necessity. International law trend and Eighth Amendment 'evolving standards' doctrine suggest norm-shift rather than discovered truth. Generated omega_international_law_constraint to bound this uncertainty. Kernel recognition is valid: three readings emit genuinely different constraints (different beneficiary/victim sets, different ε profiles, different substitutability claims).
